These vectors exercise the published [MS-PATCH LZX DELTA specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/exchange_server_protocols/ms-patch/cc78752a-b4af-4eee-88cb-01f4d8a4c2bf), revision 14.1 dated 2025-08-19. The `official-abc` vector is the exact hexadecimal example in section 3. Microsoft permits distributing specification samples for implementations in its Open Specifications copyright notice.

The remaining vectors were constructed independently by `generate_oracle.py` from sections 2.1–2.7, then decoded by unmodified upstream libmspack LZXD code. The Rust implementation was not used to generate expected bytes. Tests compare exact expected bytes; `oracle.json` retains input/output hashes and reference bytes.

Oracle source: [kyz/libmspack](https://github.com/kyz/libmspack/tree/55d501976171397ccd5d5a7a1ca7da065b1d9a06), commit `55d501976171397ccd5d5a7a1ca7da065b1d9a06`. Compiled `libmspack/mspack/{lzxd.c,system.c}` with their original `lzx.h`, `system.h`, `mspack.h`, `macros.h`, `readbits.h` and `readhuff.h`, using a small file-based harness calling `lzxd_init(system,input,output,17,0,4096,output_size,1)`, `lzxd_set_reference_data`, and `lzxd_decompress`. The harness takes five positional arguments: input, reference, output, window order, output size. Libmspack is LGPL-2.1; its source is not redistributed here.

Seven oracle comparisons all returned success and exact bytes: uncompressed `abc`, verbatim reference match, aligned reference match, and each of the four extra-length prefix forms (257, 513, 1537, 32768). These are synthetic protocol vectors, not Windows Update payloads. They establish codec interoperability with an independent decoder; they do not establish PSFX/CBS servicing or PA30 compatibility.
